action: ThaiCERT urges updating quickly to fixed versions (Enterprise 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12 or 9.4.17; Enterprise Security 8.7.0; SOAR 8.8.0 or later) and checking that pass4SymmKey in server.conf is not empty.
date_note: UzCERT says Splunk announced the issues on 18 November 2026; the Splunk advisory itself was not read.
exec: Splunk fixed 139 flaws, five rated critical, across Enterprise, Enterprise Security and SOAR; security teams running them should patch.
plain: Thailand's and Uzbekistan's cyber agencies report that Splunk fixed 139 flaws in its products, some serious enough to let attackers run code or skip logins. Neither says they are being exploited.
summary: UzCERT says Splunk announced on 18 November fixes for flaws in Splunk SOAR and Splunk Enterprise, including two SOAR remote code execution flaws rated 9.9 and 9.6, fixed in SOAR 8.8.0 or later. ThaiCERT reports the release fixes 139 vulnerabilities, five rated critical, including authentication bypasses in Enterprise REST APIs and a path traversal in Enterprise Security fixed in 8.7.0. Neither agency states exploitation.
title: Splunk fixes 139 flaws, including critical SOAR and Enterprise bugs, CERTs report

validation.note: Two independent national CERTs state the core fact: UzCERT (18 Nov) and ThaiCERT (22 Nov, read in full: 139 vulnerabilities, five critical, CVSS for CVE-2026-76535, 76536, 131202, 131253 and 131287, fixed versions, no exploitation stated). Splunk's own advisory was not read.

review.note: UzCERT page: 18 Nov Splunk announcement, SOAR RCE 9.9 and 9.6, SSO bypass high, SOAR 8.8.0+, Enterprise fixed versions list, no exploitation stated
